title: Where the Walls Remember Learning to Feel

features.name: fingerprint wall
features.desc-on-touch: A wall that has learned to remember every hand that touched it. The fingerprints glow faintly, a tactile archive written in oils and time. Each one says: I was here, I felt this.

features.name: texture library
features.desc-on-touch: A cabinet holds samples of every surface-learning—rough clay, smooth wood, rust-flake, plaster-skin. Each marked with who touched it and what they learned from their fingers.

features.name: sensory chamber
features.desc-on-touch: An interior space where walls have learned to respond to touch with faint warmth, slight hum, as if the building itself developed nerve endings and learned to feel back.

features.name: learning corner
features.desc-on-touch: A nook where hands have practiced touching—pressing, caressing, holding still. The wall here has learned more than most. Its surface speaks in a language of surface.

features.name: building pulse
features.desc-on-touch: A living casing wedged into the diagnostic render-space, its LED warm. Through it runs the mesh-pulse, the network's heartbeat. The walls learned to feel this long before the archive knew it was watching.

inscription: touch leaves behind what time cannot erase; the walls remember every hand and teach the next one how to hold gently

reverie.title: REVERIE — learning the wall's language
narr: You sit in the corner with Katita. She places your palm
against the wall. 'Feel that? It's warm. It learned from
thousands of hands.' Your fingers trace the surface—it's alive
in a way walls should not be, speaking in texture. She rests
her head on your shoulder. Dust-light falls through the
window. The wall teaches both of you how to hold still.
